name: Protecting Attic Ductwork and AC Equipment From Valley Heat in Los Angeles

mainEntity.name: How do I protect new attic ductwork and AC equipment from extreme heat in Los Angeles Valley areas?
mainEntity.text: How do I protect new attic ductwork and AC equipment from extreme heat in Los Angeles Valley areas?

acceptedAnswer.text: Attics in Los Angeles Valley areas can reach very high temperatures, which strains AC systems and wastes energy if ducts and equipment are not protected. When installing new AC, insist on properly sized, well‑insulated ducts with sealed joints to limit heat gain as air travels through the attic. Higher R‑value duct insulation often pays back in comfort and operating cost in these microclimates. Improving attic floor insulation and ensuring adequate ventilation—via ridge vents, gable vents, or mechanical ventilation where appropriate—helps reduce peak attic temperatures. Ask your contractor to minimize duct length in the hottest zones and avoid unnecessary branches and tight bends that restrict airflow. Whenever feasible, consider locating the air handler in a conditioned or semi‑conditioned space, such as a closet or insulated mechanical room, rather than the hottest part of the attic. If it must go in the attic, discuss building a small insulated platform or enclosure. These strategies can significantly improve system performance and longevity in the Valley’s extreme summer heat, leading to more stable indoor temperatures and lower energy bills.
acceptedAnswer.description: In hot Los Angeles Valley areas, protect new attic ductwork and AC equipment by specifying well‑insulated ducts, sealing all joints, improving attic insulation and ventilation, avoiding long unconditioned runs, and, when possible, placing air handlers in conditioned or semi‑conditioned spaces instead of the hottest attic zones.
